– the failing test (signature + snippet),

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test sets up a JXPathContext with variables "a"=0, "b"=0, and "c"=1. The test asserts the XPath expression "$a + $b <= $c" is true, but it fails, and the bug report states that relational operations fail when comparing a non-iterator left-hand side to an iterator right-hand side. The test basically runs the expression "0 + 0 <= 1" which should be true. The failing behavior implies the relational operator handling code does not correctly compare these values when one side is an iterator.

The test uses the JXPathContext.newContext(null) factory method, which returns an instance of JXPathContextReferenceImpl. The expression compilation leads to creation of a JXPathCompiledExpression with the compiled expression from compileExpression. This indicates the evaluation uses the JXPathCompiledExpression and relevant CoreOperation classes for relational operators.

The failure is caused because the relational operation evaluate logic incorrectly handles cases where one operand is a non-iterator (e.g., an Integer) and the other is an iterator over nodes or values, leading to wrong relational comparison results.

The problem lies within the CoreOperationRelationalExpression or CoreOperationLessThanOrEqual classes where the comparison of mixed LHS and RHS types occurs. In particular, when the LHS evaluation returns a single value and the RHS returns an iterator, the operation must properly iterate and compare or convert values before relational evaluation. The current implementation likely does a direct comparison of incompatible types, resulting in incorrect false evaluation.

No recent similar bug reports were found to confirm this, but the current failure and bug description strongly point to a missing or faulty type handling branch in relational operation evaluation logic for mixed iterator/non-iterator operands.

The next most useful step would be to inspect the evaluation logic for the CoreOperationLessThanOrEqual or CoreOperationRelationalExpression classes, specifically the evaluateCompare method or equivalent that executes the <= relational operation, to confirm the conditional handling of iterators and single values.

---
